newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian barley vote to be held Jan 23-Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: Canadian barley vote to be held Jan 23-Feb 28.

text.p: The farmer vote on whether to end the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) monopoly on Canadian barley exports will be held between January 23 and February 28, the government-appointed organizers said on Wednesday.

The Winnipeg office of KPMG Chartered Accountants, designated by Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale to administer the vote, said 80,000 ballots would be sent out on January 23. They would have to be postmarked by February 28 to qualify.
The farmers will vote on whether all types of Prairie-grown barley should be exported exclusively by the wheat board or by the private trade.

KPMG official Craig Fossay said farmers who have grown barley in the last five years will be allowed to vote. Those with CWB permit books will automatically be allowed. Those who do not have permits, for example farmers who did not export their barley, will be able to sign an affidavit to that effect.
KPMG will count the ballots and probably by the third week of March will give the results, Fossay said.

About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported, the balance fed to livestock or used in brewing in Canada. Debate has been fierce over whether farmers would be better off without the CWB.

Some farmers have criticized the fact that the question is all or nothing, not allowing a system where some grain could be exported privately and some through the CWB. But Goodale contended that a split system would be unworkable.
